P1_fx_receipts.question: Can resident individuals receive foreign currency for services or digital exports? Any conversion or repatriation rule?
P1_fx_receipts.answer: Yes. Indonesia has a free foreign-exchange regime: under Law 24/1999 Art. 2(1) every resident may freely own and use foreign exchange. FX used for domestic transactions must respect the legal-tender rules (rupiah), and Bank Indonesia may require information and data on residents' FX flows (reporting). No surrender or conversion requirement for individuals' service income was found. Indonesia's export-proceeds retention rules (DHE) cover natural-resource exporters, and they were not researched as applying to freelancers.

P2_fcy_account.question: Can individuals hold a foreign-currency bank account?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Yes. Residents may freely own foreign exchange (Law 24/1999 Art. 2(1)), so holding FX deposits at Indonesian banks is permitted. Domestic payments must generally be in rupiah.

P5_payoneer_wise.answer: Payoneer: available. Its receiving accounts include IDR, so clients can pay by local bank transfer in rupiah, and withdrawals to Indonesian banks exist (fees, minimum and timing not confirmed). Wise: Indonesia is NOT on Wise's list of countries where you can hold money.

L1_registration.question: Must an individual selling digital products or services register a business? How (sole proprietor), cost, online?
L1_registration.answer: Businesses get a Business Identification Number (NIB) through the online OSS-RBA system, the official identity for starting or running a business in Indonesia. Individuals ('orang perseorangan') register with their NIK and personal NPWP. For low-risk micro and small businesses, the NIB and a self-declaration are issued directly and can be printed. Whether a freelancer selling only to foreign clients MUST hold an NIB was not verified. Tax registration (NIK as NPWP) applies regardless (L2).

L2_tax_id.question: Tax identification number requirement and how to get it
L2_tax_id.answer: For resident individuals the NIK (national ID number) IS the NPWP (tax ID). This has been used since 14 July 2022 and fully implemented across all tax services since 1 July 2024 (PMK 136/2023 moved it from 1 Jan 2024). Old 15-digit NPWPs remain valid but the 16-digit NIK/NPWP format is mandatory in tax administration.

L3_income_tax_foreign.question: How residents' foreign-sourced or digital income is taxed
L3_income_tax_foreign.answer: Resident taxpayers are taxed on income from Indonesia AND from outside Indonesia (Income Tax Law). Small business option, PP 20/2026 (promulgated 22 Apr 2026, amending PP 55/2022): individuals can use the 0.5% final tax on gross turnover WITH NO TIME LIMIT (the old 7-year limit is gone), while turnover stays at or below Rp4.8 billion a year. Foreign turnover counts toward that limit. The first Rp500 million of an individual's turnover each year is not taxed. Transitional rules let individuals whose facility ended in 2024 or 2025 keep using it.

L3_income_tax_foreign.notes: The Income Tax Law PDF is the 2008 consolidated text; the worldwide principle wasn't found changed by UU HPP 2021 (not re-checked in consolidated form). Whether freelance 'pekerjaan bebas' professions can use the 0.5% regime: the DJP text counts turnover 'from business and services in connection with independent work' toward the limit, which suggests yes, but the eligibility exclusions (PP 55/2022 excludes some professionals) were NOT read. RE-CHECK before advising doctors, lawyers, consultants and similar.

L4_vat_gst.question: VAT/GST rate, registration threshold, treatment of exported services and digital services
L4_vat_gst.answer: VAT (PPN): 12% from 1 Jan 2025, but for non-luxury goods and services it is computed on 11/12 of the price, so 11% effective. Only luxury goods pay the full 12%. Registration as a VAT-registered business (PKP) is required only above Rp4.8 billion of gross turnover a year; smaller businesses may opt in. Exported services are 0% under PMK 32/2019 for listed services produced in Indonesia and used abroad, including IT services and many consultancy types. Two formal conditions apply: a written agreement and payment with valid proof. 0% applies only to PKPs; below the threshold no VAT is charged at all.

L5_data_protection.question: Data-protection law: name, year, in force?, regulator
L5_data_protection.answer: Personal Data Protection Law, UU 27/2022, enacted and in force 17 Oct 2022. Controllers and processors had to comply within 2 years of promulgation, i.e. by October 2024. A data protection 'lembaga' (agency) responsible to the President enforces it and imposes administrative sanctions. Whether that agency and the implementing regulations have been established was NOT confirmed.

L6_consumer_ecommerce.question: E-commerce / consumer-protection law relevant to online sales
L6_consumer_ecommerce.answer: Electronic commerce (PMSE) is governed by Government Regulation PP 80/2019 and Trade Minister Regulation Permendag 31/2023, which replaced Permendag 50/2020 in Sept 2023. Permendag 31/2023 defines marketplaces and social commerce. Social-commerce platforms may not facilitate payments in their systems (search summary). Imported finished goods sold directly cross-border into Indonesia must be priced at least US$100 per unit. Seller identity and product disclosure duties were described in a search summary but not quoted from official text.

L7_incentives.question: Government incentives or schemes for IT/digital exporters or freelancers
L7_incentives.answer: (1) PP 20/2026: individuals keep the 0.5% final tax on turnover with no time limit (up to Rp4.8bn), and the first Rp500m a year is untaxed. Spouses with separate NPWPs each get their own Rp500m. (2) No VAT registration below Rp4.8bn, plus 0% VAT on listed exported services for PKPs (L4). (3) Free foreign exchange (P1).

D1_id_document.question: Name of the national identity document residents use for identity checks
D1_id_document.answer: KTP-el (electronic Kartu Tanda Penduduk), issued through the Civil Registration Directorate (Dukcapil, Ministry of Home Affairs), carrying the NIK. A digital version (IKD, Identitas Kependudukan Digital) is also being rolled out. The NIK doubles as the tax ID (L2) and is required for OSS business registration (L1). Midtrans asks for the KTP (P3).

W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Creator income through the YouTube Partner Program (available here). (4) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (5) Physical or digital goods on Etsy (Etsy seller payments are available here). (6) Client payments by PayPal (on PayPal's Payouts list as 'Send, receive, and withdraw'). (7) Stripe lists this country as 'Preview' (sign-up by contacting Stripe sales), which is not a self-serve route for beginners yet. (8) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
